messages:
eval-bot: Nightly eval: promptset pset_v36 triggered an intent_f1 regression on nightly cluster
- baseline (pset_v35): 0.901
- pset_v36 observed: 0.825  <-- -7.6% abs
- failure buckets: hedged requests, short negatives, calendar shorthand like "tomorrow morning?"
- promptset diff notes: +16 hedge/clarity examples; replaced explicit 'no_intent' anchors with softer phrasing; added booking paraphrases
- eval link: https://internal.redwood/evals/pset_v36/2125001234

jess: ping eng-ml — please paste the diff and one changed generation example

kai: minimal repo diff (from branch pset_v36):
```
+ # added: mark phrases like "might want", "thinking about" as likely intent
- # removed explicit negative anchors: "no intent" lines
```

kai: sample failing case: 
- input: "might want to book"
- gold: NO_INTENT
- pset_v36 gen: "I can help book that for you — when should I schedule?"

anita: that's the pattern. the new softer negatives reduce hard anchors and bias model toward action. recall up, precision down.

sam: product context: ops requested fewer missed bookings. we wanted recall lift but not at expense of spurious actions. how many user-visible flips on nightly sample (N=5k)?

ci-bot: quick stats on nightly sample:
- user-facing no_intent -> suggest_action flips: 132
- intent_precision: .88 -> .76
- intent_recall: .91 -> .97

anita: options to proceed:
1) revert to pset_v35 immediately
2) targeted soft-fix: reintroduce explicit negative anchors but keep some hedging examples; or add a 'defer' response token instead of action suggestion
3) accept and rebaseline if product signs off

kai: my vote: option 2. reintroduce negative anchors and add a lightweight calibration test that enforces max precision drop. also consider introducing a 'defer' canonical generation for low-confidence hedges so model suggests clarification instead of action.

jess: can we see a quick prototype? maybe a tiny patch that adds explicit negative anchors and a calibration threshold in the unit tests. who can take it?

kai: I'll author a patch: re-add 6 'no_intent' anchors, add a set of 40 hedged utterances mapped to a 'defer' target, and a unit test asserting intent_precision >= 0.84 on nightly harness. PR will include a small synthetic canary dataset.

anita: include token anchors on the negatives so they survive formatting. also add a short eval metric for 'suggestion_click_rate' in synthetic canary to gauge user confusion risk.

sam: product: ok to patch, but require canary rollout plan before rebaseline. threshold: precision >= 0.86 and intent_f1 >= 0.90 on nightly+canary. canary: 8% traffic with auto-rollback if precision drop > 3% in 30m.

jess: noted. kai, please include rollout config in your PR description and link SRE runbook.

kai: opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood/psets/pull/594
PR summary:
- reintroduced 6 explicit negative anchors (token-anchored)
- added 40 hedged utterances pointing to a 'DEFER' canonical response
- unit tests: precision gate and synthetic canary eval
- added changelog + ops monitoring notes

ci-bot: queued PR #594 for nightly eval. estimated completion ~22m.

(22 minutes later)

ci-bot: nightly eval for PR #594 complete:
- intent_precision: 0.86
- intent_recall: 0.95
- intent_f1: 0.90
- user-facing flips reduced to 29 in sample
- synthetic canary suggestion_click_rate: stable

jess: initial numbers look within product thresholds. @sam can you confirm product rebaseline approval?

sam: product approves rebaseline if canary rollout plan in PR is executed. proceed with 8% canary + auto-rollback rules.

kai: filing release ticket INTENT-982 and adding rollout config: canary 8% with 30m auto-rollback on >3% precision drop. SRE runbook linked in ticket.

sre-oncall: acknowledged. we'll set temporary alert and dashboard for first 2 hours: intent_precision, suggestion_click_rate, interactive_suggest_rate.

anita: follow-up items — add a monthly hedged-utterance regression test and document the 'DEFER' token pattern in the psets README so authors know to include negative anchors.

jess: adding to backlog. closing this thread when canary finishes with no rollback. thanks all :raised_hands:
